tasks.notes:
Yup—you can do all of this from PowerShell. Here’s the quickest, repeatable way to (1) install GitHub CLI, (2) log in, and (3) sync/clone your repos in bulk.

# 1) Install GitHub CLI (and Git) via PowerShell

```powershell
# Run in an elevated PowerShell (Win+X → Windows Terminal (Admin))

# Prefer winget (built into Win11/most Win10)
winget install --id Git.Git -e --source winget
winget install --id GitHub.cli -e --source winget

# If winget isn’t available, Chocolatey fallback:
# Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force
# iwr https://community.chocolatey.org/install.ps1 -UseBasicParsing | iex
# choco install git gh -y
```

# 2) Authenticate the CLI

```powershell
# Start interactive login (choose HTTPS, then “Login with a web browser”)
gh auth login

# (Optional) If you prefer SSH everywhere:
# ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "you@example.com"
# gh ssh-key add "$env:USERPROFILE\.ssh\id_ed25519.pub" -t "Laptop $(hostname)"
```

# 3) One-liner to clone all repos from a user/org (new machine bootstrap)

```powershell
# Change these two:
$owner = "YourGitHubUserOrOrg"
$dest  = "$HOME\Dev"    # where you want them

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $dest -Force | Out-Null
cd $dest

# Requires gh CLI 2.x
gh repo list $owner --limit 200 --json name,sshUrl,cloneUrl | `
  ConvertFrom-Json | ForEach-Object {
    $dir = Join-Path $dest $_.name
    if (Test-Path $dir) {
      Write-Host "Skipping existing repo $($_.name)"
    } else {
      # Use SSH if you set that up; otherwise use cloneUrl (HTTPS)
      git clone ($_.sshUrl ?? $_.cloneUrl)
    }
  }
```

# 4) “Sync everything” for repos you already have locally

This walks a directory, finds every Git repo, fetches/prunes, and fast-forwards the default branch.

```powershell
function Sync-Repos {
  param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)][string]$Root,
    [string]$DefaultBranch = "main"   # change to "master" if needed
  )

  Get-ChildItem -Path $Root -Directory -Recurse -Depth 2 | Where-Object {
    Test-Path (Join-Path $_.FullName ".git")
  } | ForEach-Object {
    $repo = $_.FullName
    Write-Host "`n=== $repo ==="
    Push-Location $repo
    try {
      git remote -v
      git fetch --all --prune
      # If the default branch exists, fast-forward it
      if (git show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/$DefaultBranch") {
        git checkout $DefaultBranch
        git pull --ff-only
      }
      # Update any tracking branches without switching to them
      git for-each-ref --format="%(refname:short)" refs/heads | ForEach-Object {
        git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name "$_@{upstream}" *> $null
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { git branch --ff-only $_ } 
      }
    } finally {
      Pop-Location
    }
  }
}

# Use it:
# Sync-Repos -Root "$HOME\Dev" -DefaultBranch main
```

# 5) (Optional) Set sane global Git defaults once

```powershell
git config --global user.name  "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
git config --global pull.ff only
git config --global init.defaultBranch main
git config --global core.autocrlf true
# Windows Credential Manager (HTTPS auth caching)
git config --global credential.helper manager-core
```

## TL;DR

* Yes, you can do everything in PowerShell.

```python
        status_scroll.grid(row=0, column=1, sticky=(tk.N, tk.S))

        # Action Buttons
        button_frame = ttk.Frame(main_frame)
        button_frame.grid(row=3, column=0, columnspan=3, pady=20)
        
        ttk.Button(button_frame, text="Backup Current Config",

        ttk.Button(button_frame, text="Apply Security Config",

        ttk.Button(button_frame, text="Run Leak Test",

        # Progress bar

    def log_status(self, message):
        """Add message to status log"""
        self.status_text.insert(tk.END, f"{message}\n")
        self.status_text.see(tk.END)

    def refresh_vpn_interfaces(self):
        """Refresh the list of available VPN interfaces"""
        self.log_status("Scanning for VPN interfaces...")
        interfaces = self.network_detector.get_vpn_interfaces()
        
        self.vpn_combo['values'] = [f"{name} ({ip})" for name, ip in interfaces]
        if interfaces:
            self.vpn_combo.current(0)
            self.log_status(f"Found {len(interfaces)} VPN interface(s)")
        else:
            self.log_status("⚠️ No VPN interfaces detected. Please connect to VPN first.")
    
    def backup_config(self):
        """Backup current qBittorrent configuration"""
        try:
            backup_path = self.config_manager.backup_config()
            self.log_status(f"✅ Configuration backed up to: {backup_path}")
            messagebox.showinfo("Backup Complete", f"Configuration saved to:\n{backup_path}")
        except Exception as e:
            self.log_status(f"❌ Backup failed: {str(e)}")
            messagebox.showerror("Backup Failed", str(e))
    
    def apply_security(self):

        if not self.vpn_var.get():
            messagebox.showerror("Error", "Please select a VPN interface first")

        def apply_config():
            try:
                self.progress.start()
                interface_info = self.vpn_var.get()
                interface_name = interface_info.split(' (')[0]
                
                self.log_status("Applying security configuration...")
                self.config_manager.apply_security_config(interface_name)
                self.log_status("✅ Security configuration applied successfully!")
                
                messagebox.showinfo("Success", "Security configuration applied!\nRestart qBittorrent to activate changes.")
            except Exception as e:
                self.log_status(f"❌ Configuration failed: {str(e)}")
                messagebox.showerror("Configuration Failed", str(e))
            finally:
                self.progress.stop()
        
        threading.Thread(target=apply_config, daemon=True).start()
    
    def run_leak_test(self):
        """Run comprehensive leak testing"""
        def test_leaks():
            try:
                self.progress.start()
                self.log_status("Starting comprehensive leak test...")
                
                results = self.security_tester.run_full_test()
                
                for test_name, result in results.items():
                    status = "✅" if result['passed'] else "❌"
                    self.log_status(f"{status} {test_name}: {result['message']}")
                
                overall_passed = all(r['passed'] for r in results.values())
                if overall_passed:
                    self.log_status("🎉 All security tests PASSED!")
                    messagebox.showinfo("Test Results", "All security tests passed!\nYour configuration is secure.")
                else:
                    self.log_status("⚠️ Some tests FAILED. Review results above.")
                    messagebox.showwarning("Test Results", "Some security tests failed.\nCheck the log for details.")
                    
            except Exception as e:
                self.log_status(f"❌ Testing failed: {str(e)}")
                messagebox.showerror("Test Failed", str(e))
            finally:
                self.progress.stop()
        
        threading.Thread(target=test_leaks, daemon=True).start()
    
    def generate_report(self):
        """Generate security report"""
        try:
            report_path = self.report_generator.create_report()
            self.log_status(f"📊 Security report generated: {report_path}")
            
            if messagebox.askyesno("Report Generated", f"Report saved to:\n{report_path}\n\nOpen report now?"):
                os.startfile(report_path)  # Windows
                
        except Exception as e:
            self.log_status(f"❌ Report generation failed: {str(e)}")
            messagebox.showerror("Report Failed", str(e))

def main():
    """Main application entry point"""
    root = tk.Tk()
    app = QBTSecurityGUI(root)
    root.mainloop()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

### **network_detector.py** - VPN Interface Detection
```python
"""
Network interface detection and VPN identification
"""

import psutil
import netifaces
import socket
import subprocess
import platform
import re
from typing import List, Tuple, Dict, Optional

class NetworkDetector:
    def __init__(self):
        self.system = platform.system().lower()
        self.vpn_patterns = [
            r'nord',
            r'express',
            r'tap',
            r'tun',
            r'vpn',
            r'wireguard',
            r'openvpn',
            r'pptp',
            r'l2tp'
        ]
    
    def get_vpn_interfaces(self) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
        """
        Detect VPN interfaces and their IP addresses
        Returns: List of (interface_name, ip_address) tuples
        """
        vpn_interfaces = []
        
        try:
            # Get all network interfaces
            interfaces = psutil.net_if_addrs()
            
            for interface_name, addresses in interfaces.items():
                if self._is_vpn_interface(interface_name):
                    ipv4_addr = self._get_ipv4_address(addresses)
                    if ipv4_addr and self._is_interface_active(interface_name):
                        vpn_interfaces.append((interface_name, ipv4_addr))
            
            # Sort by preference (NordLynx, then others)
            vpn_interfaces.sort(key=lambda x: (
                0 if 'nord' in x[0].lower() else
                1 if 'express' in x[0].lower() else
                2
            ))
            
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error detecting VPN interfaces: {e}")
        
        return vpn_interfaces
    
    def _is_vpn_interface(self, interface_name: str) -> bool:
        """Check if interface name matches VPN patterns"""
        name_lower = interface_name.lower()
        return any(re.search(pattern, name_lower) for pattern in self.vpn_patterns)
    
    def _get_ipv4_address(self, addresses) -> Optional[str]:
        """Extract IPv4 address from interface addresses"""
        for addr in addresses:
            if addr.family == socket.AF_INET:
                return addr.address
        return None
    
    def _is_interface_active(self, interface_name: str) -> bool:
        """Check if network interface is active/up"""
        try:
            stats = psutil.net_if_stats().get(interface_name)
            return stats and stats.isup
        except:
            return False
    
    def get_current_external_ip(self) -> Optional[str]:
        """Get current external IP address"""
        try:
            import requests
            response = requests.get('https://api.ipify.org', timeout=5)
            return response.text.strip()
        except:
            return None
    
    def get_interface_details(self, interface_name: str) -> Dict:
        """Get detailed information about a specific interface"""
        details = {
            'name': interface_name,
            'active': False,
            'ipv4': None,
            'ipv6': None,
            'mac': None,
            'mtu': None
        }
        
        try:
            # Get addresses
            if interface_name in psutil.net_if_addrs():
                addresses = psutil.net_if_addrs()[interface_name]
                for addr in addresses:
                    if addr.family == socket.AF_INET:
                        details['ipv4'] = addr.address
                    elif addr.family == socket.AF_INET6:
                        details['ipv6'] = addr.address
                    elif addr.family == psutil.AF_LINK:
                        details['mac'] = addr.address
            
            # Get stats
            if interface_name in psutil.net_if_stats():
                stats = psutil.net_if_stats()[interface_name]
                details['active'] = stats.isup
                details['mtu'] = stats.mtu
            
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error getting interface details: {e}")
        
        return details
    
    def validate_vpn_connection(self, interface_name: str) -> Dict:
        """Validate that VPN connection is working properly"""
        validation = {
            'interface_active': False,
            'has_ip': False,
            'external_ip_matches': False,
            'dns_working': False,
            'overall_status': False
        }
        
        try:
            # Check interface is active
            details = self.get_interface_details(interface_name)
            validation['interface_active'] = details['active']
            validation['has_ip'] = bool(details['ipv4'])
            
            if validation['has_ip']:
                # Check if external IP is different from local IP (indicating VPN)
                external_ip = self.get_current_external_ip()
                if external_ip and external_ip != details['ipv4']:
                    validation['external_ip_matches'] = True
                
                # Test DNS resolution
                try:
                    socket.gethostbyname('google.com')
                    validation['dns_working'] = True
                except:
                    pass
            
            # Overall status
            validation['overall_status'] = all([
                validation['interface_active'],
                validation['has_ip'],
                validation['dns_working']
            ])
            
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error validating VPN connection: {e}")
        
        return validation

# Test the detector
if __name__ == "__main__":
    detector = NetworkDetector()
    interfaces = detector.get_vpn_interfaces()
    
    print("Detected VPN Interfaces:")
    for name, ip in interfaces:
        print(f"  {name}: {ip}")
        
        # Get detailed info
        details = detector.get_interface_details(name)
        print(f"    Active: {details['active']}")
        print(f"    MAC: {details['mac']}")
        print(f"    MTU: {details['mtu']}")
        
        # Validate connection
        validation = detector.validate_vpn_connection(name)
        print(f"    Validation: {validation['overall_status']}")
        print()
```

function Get-PSHangReport {
  param([int]$Id)

  $p  = Get-Process -Id $Id -ErrorAction Stop
  $ci = Get-CimInstance Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfProc_Process -Filter "IDProcess=$Id"

  # Basic footprint
  $snap = [pscustomobject]@{
    Time    = (Get-Date)
    PID     = $p.Id
    Name    = $p.ProcessName
    Respond = $p.Responding
    CPU_s   = '{0:n3}' -f $p.CPU
    CPUpct  = '{0:n1}' -f $ci.PercentProcessorTime
    WS_MB   = [int]($p.WorkingSet64/1MB)
    PM_MB   = [int]($p.PrivateMemorySize64/1MB)
    Handles = $p.Handles
    Threads = $p.Threads.Count
    IOR_MB  = '{0:n1}' -f ($p.IOReadBytes/1MB)
    IOW_MB  = '{0:n1}' -f ($p.IOWriteBytes/1MB)
    IOO_MB  = '{0:n1}' -f ($p.IOOtherBytes/1MB)
  }

  # Thread wait reasons (what are we waiting on?)
  $tw = $p.Threads | Group-Object WaitReason | Sort Count -Desc |
        Select @{n='WaitReason';e={$_.Name}}, Count

  # Top CPU threads (if it’s hot)
  $topT = $p.Threads | Sort TotalProcessorTime -Desc | Select -First 5 `
          Id, TotalProcessorTime, PriorityLevel, ThreadState, WaitReason

  # Sockets owned by this process (network hangs show up here)
  $tcp = Get-NetTCPConnection -OwningProcess $Id -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
         Group-Object State | Sort Count -Desc |
         Select @{n='TCPState';e={$_.Name}}, Count

  # Quick verdict hints
  $hint =
    if ([double]$ci.PercentProcessorTime -gt 50) { 'CPU-bound (tight loop or runaway work)' }
    elseif ($tw | ? WaitReason -match 'IOCompletion|PageIn|Suspended') { 'Waiting on I/O (disk/net/pipe) or suspended' }
    elseif ($tcp | ? TCPState -in 'SYN_SENT','CLOSE_WAIT','TIME_WAIT') { 'Likely blocked on a socket (remote slow/closed)' }
    elseif (-not $p.Responding) { 'GUI nonresponsive—message pump blocked' }
    else { 'Low CPU + waiting threads → benign wait or external dependency' }

  [pscustomobject]@{
    Summary = $snap
    ThreadWaits = $tw
    TopThreads  = $topT
    TCPStates   = $tcp
    Hint        = $hint
  }
}

# 12 Best Logging Practices

## Introduction
- Importance of logging for debugging, monitoring, and maintaining software.
- Common pitfalls when logging is done poorly.
- **Goals:** Ensure logs are actionable, concise, and valuable.

---

## 12 Best Practices for Logging

1. **Log Contextual Information**
   - Include relevant metadata (e.g., user ID, session ID, request ID).
   - Helps correlate logs across systems and trace issues effectively.

2. **Use Structured Logging**
   - Avoid plain-text logs; use structured formats like JSON.
   - Structured logs are machine-readable, enabling better querying and analysis.

3. **Log at the Right Level**
   - Define appropriate log levels: `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARN`, `ERROR`, `FATAL`.
   - Avoid overusing `DEBUG` or `INFO`, and ensure errors are flagged correctly.

4. **Avoid Logging Sensitive Data**
   - Do not log passwords, API keys, or Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
   - Anonymize or redact sensitive data if necessary.

5. **Be Consistent in Log Formatting**
   - Adopt a standard format for log messages across the team/project.
   - Consistency improves readability and simplifies parsing.

6. **Include Timestamps**
   - Always log events with precise timestamps, including time zones.
   - Helps in analyzing the sequence of events accurately.

7. **Log Errors with Stack Traces**
   - Provide detailed stack traces for exceptions and errors.
   - Stack traces aid in pinpointing the root cause of issues.

8. **Log Inputs and Outputs**
   - Capture input parameters and output results of critical operations.
   - This ensures visibility into what the system is processing.

9. **Use Transaction IDs**
   - Assign unique IDs to correlate logs for a single transaction or request.
   - Essential for tracing multi-service workflows in distributed systems.

10. **Control Log Volume**
    - Avoid excessive logging to prevent performance degradation and bloated logs.
    - Use sampling or rate-limiting for repetitive logs.

11. **Centralize Your Logs**
    - Use log aggregation tools like ELK Stack, Splunk, or Fluentd.
    - Centralized logs make searching, filtering, and analysis more efficient.

12. **Regularly Review and Clean Logs**
    - Audit logs periodically for relevance and accuracy.
    - Remove outdated or redundant log statements.

---

## Conclusion
- Good logging practices enhance maintainability, debugging, and observability.
- Balancing verbosity and performance is crucial.
- Regularly revisit your logging strategy to ensure it meets evolving needs.

Here's a comprehensive Git branching strategy that balances flexibility and structure:

### Recommended Branch Structure

1. **Main Branches:**
- `main` (or `master`): Stable, production-ready code
- `develop`: Integration branch for ongoing development

2. **Supporting Branches:**
- `feature/`: Individual feature development
- `release/`: Preparing for a new production release
- `hotfix/`: Urgent production bug fixes
- `delta/`: Experimental or significant architectural changes

### Workflow Details

#### Main Branch Flow
```
main (production code)
│
└── develop (integration branch)
    │
    ├── feature/authentication
    ├── feature/payment-gateway
    └── release/v1.2.0
```

#### Typical Process
1. Create features from `develop`
2. Merge completed features back to `develop`
3. Create `release/` branch from `develop` for final testing
4. Merge `release/` into `main` and `develop`
5. Tag the release in `main`

#### Hotfix Example
```
main
│
└── hotfix/critical-security-patch
    └── merged back to main & develop
```

### Best Practices
- Use semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH)
- Enforce code reviews
- Automate CI/CD pipelines
- Keep `main` always deployable
- Use descriptive branch names

### Recommended Tools
- Git Flow
- GitHub Flow
- GitLab Flow

The phrase "Cut failed changes by 30%" typically means to reduce the number of failed changes by 30%. 

In a business or technical context, "changes" often refer to modifications made to a system, process, or product. "Failed changes" would then refer to changes that did not succeed, which could be due to various reasons such as errors, bugs, or unintended consequences.

To "cut" failed changes by 30% means to decrease their number by 30% compared to a previous baseline or target. For example, if there were 100 failed changes previously, cutting them by 30% would result in 70 failed changes.

This phrase is often used in the context of quality improvement, process optimization, or reliability engineering, where reducing the number of failed changes is a key goal. 

For instance, if a company has a change failure rate of 10%, and they want to improve it, they might set a goal to "cut failed changes by 30%", which would translate to reducing the change failure rate to 7%. 

In mathematical terms, this can be represented as: 
Let $x$ be the original number of failed changes. 
Cutting failed changes by 30% can be represented as: $$x - 0.3x = 0.7x$$ 
Which means the new number of failed changes is 70% of the original number, or 30% less.

# Define the repository name and description
$repoName = "SysAdminSuite"
$repoDescription = "A collection of IT tools for configs, installs, printer mapping, remote solutions, and tests."

# Create a new directory for the repository
$repoPath = "C:\path\to\your\repositories\$repoName"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $repoPath

# Initialize a new Git repository
Set-Location -Path $repoPath
git init

# Create a README file
$readmeContent = @"
# $repoName

$repoDescription

## Table of Contents

- [Configs](#configs)
- [Installs](#installs)
- [Printer Mapping](#printer-mapping)
- [Remote Solutions](#remote-solutions)
- [Tests](#tests)

## Configs

## Installs

## Printer Mapping

## Remote Solutions

## Tests
"@
$readmeContent | Out-File -FilePath "README.md" -Encoding utf8

# Add the README file to the repository
git add README.md

# Commit the initial files
git commit -m "Initial commit"

# Create a new private repository on GitHub
gh repo create $repoName --private --description "$repoDescription"

# Add the GitHub repository as a remote
$githubUrl = "https://github.com/your-username/$repoName.git"
git remote add origin $githubUrl

# Push the initial commit to the GitHub repository

tasks.notes:
# Cleanup script for stray/bad filenames in Git branches
# Usage: run from the repo root, already cloned locally

# 1) Make sure you’re on the branch and up to date
git fetch --prune
git checkout <branch-name>
git pull --ff-only

# 2) See suspicious files in the index
git ls-files | egrep '(^tatus$|^status$|porcelain|git checkout main|ersCheeks)'

# 3) Remove the obvious ones (won’t error if they’re missing)
git rm -f -- 'tatus' || true
git rm -f -- 'tatus --porcelain' || true
git rm -f -- 'status' || true

# 4) Find & remove any weird long filename containing "git checkout main"
WEIRD="$(git ls-files | grep -F 'git checkout main' || true)"
if [ -n "$WEIRD" ]; then
  echo "Removing: $WEIRD"
  git rm -f -- "$WEIRD"
fi

# 5) Commit and push
git commit -m "chore: remove stray debug/status files with spaces/non-ASCII (cleanup)"
git push -u origin <branch-name>

# 6) Quick sanity check
git log -1 --name-status

On Windows 11, the equivalent of running `sudo` on Linux or macOS is to start **PowerShell with elevated (administrator) privileges**.
Here’s how you can do it:

**Method 1 – From Start Menu**

1. Press **Windows Key** and type **PowerShell**.
2. Right-click **Windows PowerShell** (or **Windows Terminal** if you’re using that).
3. Select **Run as administrator**.
4. Click **Yes** on the UAC (User Account Control) prompt.

**Method 2 – From Run Dialog**

1. Press **Windows + R** to open Run.
2. Type:

   ```
   powershell
   ```
3. Press **Ctrl + Shift + Enter** instead of just Enter — this runs it as admin.

**Method 3 – Inside an Existing PowerShell Window**
If you’re already in a non-admin PowerShell window and want to relaunch as admin, run:

```powershell
Start-Process powershell -Verb runAs
```

You’ll get a new elevated window after confirming the UAC prompt.

If you want, I can also show you **how to set PowerShell to always open as admin** so you don’t have to do this each time.

To alter the hotkeys for the cursor in Neovim and prevent them from reverting to the default settings, you can customize your configuration file. Here’s how to do it:

## 🛠️ Customizing Hotkeys in Neovim

### Step 1: Open Your Configuration File
1. Open Neovim.
2. Access your configuration file, typically located at `~/.config/nvim/init.vim` or `~/.config/nvim/init.lua` depending on whether you are using Vimscript or Lua.

### Step 2: Set Custom Key Mappings
You can set custom key mappings in your configuration file. Here’s how to do it for both Vimscript and Lua:

#### For Vimscript (`init.vim`)
```vim
" Example of custom key mappings
nnoremap <C-j> j  " Move cursor down
nnoremap <C-k> k  " Move cursor up
nnoremap <C-h> h  " Move cursor left
nnoremap <C-l> l  " Move cursor right
```

#### For Lua (`init.lua`)
```lua
-- Example of custom key mappings
vim.api.nvim_set_keymap('n', '<C-j>', 'j', { noremap = true, silent = true })  -- Move cursor down
vim.api.nvim_set_keymap('n', '<C-k>', 'k', { noremap = true, silent = true })  -- Move cursor up
vim.api.nvim_set_keymap('n', '<C-h>', 'h', { noremap = true, silent = true })  -- Move cursor left
vim.api.nvim_set_keymap('n', '<C-l>', 'l', { noremap = true, silent = true })  -- Move cursor right
```

### Step 3: Save and Reload
After making your changes, save the configuration file and reload Neovim. You can also run `:source %` in Neovim to reload the configuration without restarting.

### Step 4: Check for Conflicts
If your custom hotkeys still revert to the defaults, check for any plugins or settings that might be overriding your mappings. You can also use the command `:verbose map` to see all current mappings and their sources.

By following these steps, you should be able to customize your cursor hotkeys in Neovim effectively. If you have any specific hotkeys in mind or need further assistance, feel free to ask!

tasks.notes:
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Lists saved WLAN profiles and their passwords.
.DESCRIPTION
Uses 'netsh wlan show profiles' to find saved Wi-Fi networks and then
'netsh wlan show profile name="<Profile Name>" key=clear' to retrieve the password
for each profile. Skips profiles that are likely system-managed (like Intel or Cisco).
Displays profile names and their passwords.
.NOTES
Requires Administrator privileges to see key content on some systems/profiles,
though often works without for user-saved profiles.
Enterprise passwords (802.1X) are not retrievable this way.
#>

Write-Host "Retrieving saved Wi-Fi profiles and passwords..."

# Get list of WLAN profiles, filter out some common non-user profiles
$profiles = netsh wlan show profiles |
    Select-String -Pattern ": (.*)$" |
    ForEach-Object {$_.Matches.Groups[1].Value.Trim()} |
    Where-Object {$_ -notmatch "Intel|Cisco|Group Policy|Additional"} # Add more filters if needed

if ($profiles.Count -eq 0) {
    Write-Host "No saved Wi-Fi profiles found."
} else {
    Write-Host "`n--- Saved Profiles and Passwords ---`n"

    foreach ($profile in $profiles) {
        Write-Host "Profile Name: $($profile)"
        try {
            # Get profile details including key in clear text
            $profileDetails = netsh wlan show profile name="$profile" key=clear
            $passwordLine = $profileDetails | Select-String -Pattern "Key Content            : (.*)$"

            if ($passwordLine) {
                $password = $passwordLine.Matches.Groups[1].Value.Trim()
                Write-Host "Password: $($password)" -ForegroundColor Green
            } else {
                Write-Host "Password: Not found or not stored in plain text." -ForegroundColor Yellow
            }
        } catch {
            Write-Host "Error retrieving details for $($profile): $($_.Exception.Message)" -ForegroundColor Red
        }
        Write-Host "" # Add a blank line for separation
    }
    Write-Host "--- End of List ---"
}

A "25% reduction in variance across sites" means that the variance, or the spread, of a particular metric or measurement across different sites is reduced by 25%.

In statistical terms, variance measures how much individual data points deviate from the average value. A reduction in variance indicates that the data points are becoming more consistent or homogeneous across sites.

For example, let's say you're measuring the average customer satisfaction score across different stores. If the variance is high, it means that some stores have very high satisfaction scores, while others have very low scores. A 25% reduction in variance would mean that the spread of these scores is reduced, so that the scores are more consistent across stores.

In mathematical terms, if the original variance is $\sigma^2$, a 25% reduction in variance can be represented as: 
$$0.75\sigma^2$$

This means that the new variance is 75% of the original variance, or 25% less.

For instance, if the original variance is 100, a 25% reduction would result in a new variance of: 
$$0.75 \times 100 = 75$$

So, the variance is reduced from 100 to 75, which is a 25% reduction.

tasks.notes:
That's a great approach! Injecting humor can definitely help ease tension. Here are some other humorous ways to greet your boss, playing on similar themes of anticipation, news, or a lighthearted take on the workday:

**Playing on "Good News":**

*   "What fresh hell... I mean, *exciting challenge* awaits?"
*   "Ready for my daily dose of delightful directives!"
*   "Don't tell me... another opportunity for greatness?"
*   "Just when I thought my day couldn't get any more thrilling..."

**Lighthearted Takes on the Workday:**

*   "Here to make your day slightly less chaotic, or at least add to the chaos in an entertaining way."
*   "Reporting for duty, and by 'duty' I mean ready for coffee and a good challenge."
*   "Is it five o'clock yet? Just kidding (mostly)."
*   "Survived another commute. What's on the agenda for today's gladiatorial arena?"

**Slightly Absurd/Unexpected:**

*   (If you have a prop, even a pen) "My crystal ball told me you'd be looking for me!"
*   "Did someone say... *synergy*?" (Said with mock enthusiasm)
*   "I've perfected my 'busy but available' look just for you."
*   "What's the haps, chief?"

**Things to Keep in Mind:**

*   **Know your boss:** While humor is good, make sure it aligns with their personality and the company culture. What works for one boss might not for another.
*   **Delivery is key:** Your tone and a genuine smile will sell the humor.
*   **Don't overdo it:** Like your original phrase, these can get thin if used every single time. Mix them up, or use them when the situation calls for a little levity.
*   **Read the room:** If your boss is clearly in a serious mood or dealing with a crisis, it might be best to stick to a more standard greeting.

Choose the one that feels most natural for you and your relationship with your boss!

Debugging and adjusting: It’s impossible to reason about and debug why the LLM made a given decision, which means it’s very hard to change how it makes those decisions if you need to tweak them. You don’t understand the journey it took through the high-dimensional semantic space to get to your answer, and it’s really poor at explaining it too. Even purpose-built neural networks like those in chess engines can be challenging for observability, and a general LLM is a nightmare, despite Anthropic’s great strides in this area

And the rest…: testing LLM outputs is much harder than unit-testing known code-paths; LLMs are much worse at math than your CPU; LLMs are insufficiently good at picking random numbers; version-control and auditing becomes much harder; monitoring and observability gets painful; state management through natural language is fragile; you’re at the mercy of API rate limits and costs; and security boundaries become fuzzy when everything flows through prompts.

tasks.notes:
Short answer: if the LLC site is on Squarespace, the sitemap is automatic and free. No add-on, no upsell.

Details:

* Squarespace autogenerates and maintains `https://yourdomain.com/sitemap.xml` for all public pages. It updates as you publish/unpublish and respects pages you hide from search. Zero effort, zero cost.
* Even if we don’t use Squarespace, a sitemap is a trivial deliverable. For a 5-page MVP it’s a 5-minute `sitemap.xml` (plus `robots.txt`)—this should never be a line-item.

My stance for the MVP: I’ll include a valid `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt` in scope at no extra cost, and wire basic SEO hygiene:

* page titles + meta descriptions
* canonical tags
* open graph/Twitter cards
* clean URLs + 301s (if needed)

If you want “SEO setup” beyond that (Search Console/Bing Webmaster verification, XML feed tweaks, schema markup, analytics goals), that’s a small “go-live” checklist we can tack on—but the sitemap itself is covered. Next step: lock platform (Squarespace vs custom). I’ll bake the sitemap in either way.

MapWL244_ENT06X.vbs – maps \\SWBPNSHPS01V\WL244-ENT06X
'                       or falls back to IP_10.137.67.158,
'                       using Xerox Global Print Driver PCL6 V5.860.8.0.
Option Explicit

Const QUEUE = "\\SWBPNSHPS01V\WL244-ENT06X"
Const IP    = "10.137.67.158"
Const PORT  = "IP_" & IP
Const PRN   = "WL244-ENT06X"
Const DRV   = "Xerox Global Print Driver PCL6 V5.860.8.0"   ' ← exact driver name

Dim net : Set net = CreateObject("WScript.Network")
Dim sh  : Set sh  = CreateObject("WScript.Shell")
On Error Resume Next

'──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
' 1) Try the normal print-server queue
'──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
net.AddWindowsPrinterConnection QUEUE
If Err.Number = 0 Then SelfDeleteAndQuit

'──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
' 2) Create Standard TCP/IP port via WMI  (no prnport.vbs needed)
'──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Err.Clear
Dim svc : Set svc = GetObject("winmgmts:{impersonationLevel=impersonate}!\\.\root\cimv2")
Dim p   : Set p   = svc.Get("Win32_TCPIPPrinterPort").SpawnInstance_
p.Name        = PORT
p.Protocol    = 1            ' RAW
p.HostAddress = IP
p.PortNumber  = 9100
p.SNMPEnabled = False
p.Put_

'──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
' 3) Add the printer on that port
'──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
sh.Run "rundll32 printui.dll,PrintUIEntry /if /b """ & PRN & _
       """ /r " & PORT & " /m """ & DRV & """ /z /q", 0, True

SelfDeleteAndQuit

'──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Sub SelfDeleteAndQuit
    ' Remove script from Startup after successful mapping.
    On Error Resume Next
    sh.DeleteFile WScript.ScriptFullName
    WScript.Quit 0
End Sub
